- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 5–10 day horizon.
- If official event net supply is strongly bearish (net < -20) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts when price moves >10% from 18d average; cap forecast at 1.5x recent average unless driven by strong bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model often fails to capture downward pressure; apply 5–10% downward correction for 30d horizon.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent spikes; smooth forecast curve by reducing slope after 3–5 consecutive days of high price.
